answer: In an agent economy, each participant must compute a personalized delta from its long-term private key and the current epoch seed, then publish a zero-knowledge proof of that computation. Peers mirror the resulting commitment into a karst of append-only logs. An attacker creating many identities faces linear growth in private-key storage and proof generation cost, while the karst forces every mirror step to be publicly verifiable, making bulk Sybil creation economically prohibitive.
